question:
Triangle \(ABC\) is an isosceles triangle with \(\overline{AB}=\overline{BC}.\) Point \(D\) is the midpoint of both \(\overline{BC}\) and \(\overline{AE},\) and \(\overline{CE}\) is \(11\) units long. Triangle \(ABD\) is congruent to triangle \(ECD.\) What is the length of \(\overline{BD}?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2006_AMC_8_Q19_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The given congruence transfers the known length to a side of triangle \(ABC\). In \(\triangle ABD\cong\triangle ECD\), side \(AB\) corresponds to side \(EC\), so
\[
AB=EC=11.
\]
Since \(AB=BC\), we also have \(BC=11\). Point \(D\) is the midpoint of \(BC\), so it divides that segment into two equal lengths. Therefore
\[
BD=\frac{BC}{2}=\frac{11}{2}=5.5.
\]
The length is \(5.5\) units, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
